name: Overlapping Community Detection by k-Clique Percolation
problem_statement: Find overlapping communities formed by connected components of the clique-adjacency graph, where two k-cliques are adjacent when they share k-1 vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: k
problem_inputs.description: Clique size used to construct the clique-adjacency graph.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_community_size
problem_inputs.description: Minimum number of distinct original vertices in a returned community.

problem_inputs.name: include_unassigned_vertices
problem_inputs.description: Report vertices that belong to no qualifying k-clique.

required_outputs.name: communities
required_outputs.description: Unique community IDs with the union of vertices in each k-clique component.

required_outputs.name: community_ids_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Zero or more community memberships per vertex.

optional_outputs.name: member_k_cliques_by_community
optional_outputs.description: The k-cliques whose adjacency component defines each community.

optional_outputs.name: unassigned_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Vertices belonging to no returned community.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute all connected components in the graph of k-cliques linked by k-1 shared vertices.
solution_semantics.exactness: All qualifying k-cliques and their components are computed exactly.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Equivalent vertex-union communities produced by distinct clique components remain distinct only if their defining components differ; each component is returned once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Community IDs and ordering are arbitrary.

validation_rules: Every member k-clique is a valid size-k clique.
All cliques in a community are connected through k-1 overlap steps.
No two returned communities belong to the same clique-adjacency component.
Membership maps agree with community vertex sets.
edge_cases: If the graph contains no k-cliques, there are no communities.
For k=2, communities correspond to nontrivial connected edge components.
A vertex may belong to multiple communities.
